**To the mayor, from `matt561`: `flutter/flutter#196561`, branch `vcfix-manifest-fallback`**

The KDoc fix is committed locally on top of `f3d2ab1fd3b` and not pushed. I ran nothing after the two emulator runs below, so I don't have the new commit's SHA, any definition-of-done output, or CI results. Before you can push, I need to run the steps in **Next steps**.

**What I found (API 35 emulator, built with `--split-per-abi -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true`, no `versionCode` in `android {}` or the manifest)**
- **Fresh install:** `adb uninstall`, then `adb install app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` gives `Success`. `dumpsys package` shows `versionCode=0`.
- **Install over a build with `versionCode=7`:** `adb install -r` of the same APK gives `Failure [INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE]`.
- **Other ABIs:** In `configureSplitPerAbiVersionCodes`, the flag returns before any output's `versionCode` is set. So every split APK gets the same value. I checked the 0 with `dumpsys` on arm64 only.

So "Android refuses to install" is false, and @mboetger is right. The flag builds APKs that all have `versionCode` 0. They install on a device that doesn't have the app. They fail as a downgrade over any installed build with a higher `versionCode`. They also share one `versionCode`, which is the case the error message already says Google Play rejects.

**Draft reply to @mboetger (human reviewer, so I did not post it; saved locally at `replies/r4606860038.md`)**
> You're right. With `force-version-code-ignoring-abi` and no `versionCode` set, every split APK gets `versionCode` 0. On an API 35 emulator, `adb install` onto a device without the app succeeds (`dumpsys` shows `versionCode=0`). `adb install -r` over a `versionCode=7` build fails with `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE`. <new-sha> rewrites the KDoc to say this. It still doesn't suggest the flag, because the splits share `versionCode` 0, which Play rejects, and they can't upgrade an existing install.

**Decisions for you to check**
1. **Should the error message still leave out the flag?** I kept it out. `versionCode = flutter.versionCode` is a one-line fix that gives correct codes, and the flag leads users to `versionCode` 0 builds that can't upgrade an installed app. The other option is to mention the flag as a local-testing-only workaround. Only the KDoc changed; the code behaves as before.
2. **Narrower wording.** The old text said "no positive `versionCode`". I tested only a missing `versionCode`, so the new text says "sets no `versionCode`". I didn't test `versionCode="0"` or a negative value.
3. **Test coverage.** I tested only API 35 on one emulator. I didn't add or change any tests.

Nothing here is hard to undo, because nothing is pushed. If reidbaker had approved before this commit, a push would need his re-approval.
